institutionName: University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have family connections in this city, and I am considering moving in here for the future, so having an exchange here was a wonderful opportunity for networking and getting to know the academic and working culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *

questions.answer: There were information sessions during the info days, the website provided a lot of information and checklist about practical information as well.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have participated in the info days, and I had a buddy as well to assist in specific questions

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I have applied 3 months early for accommodation, which was the reason that I could find a cheap room - the places fill up fast in most student housings.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Both BOKU campuses that are in the city are easily accessible through public transport

Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process is comparable to total anarchy. The places are filling up very quick, but that doesn't matter, because the courses still might or might not be held at an uncertain time schedule. Personal connection to the lecturers is very essential, because even if not registered, it is possible to get a place in the course if asked nicely. It is impossible to avoid clash of courses at 30 credits, and the workload is always uneven, because the schedule is not known at the time of registration.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The lecturers and the administration were always happy to help and they were responsive, even if they couldn't always answer questions, a solution could be found to every problem.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: At the end, I managed to register and finish all the courses in my learning agreement, but it was very stressful and uncertain (one course's timetable wasn't fixed until May, and it was held at the end of June, at the last week of the semester)

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register for more courses than it is stated in the learning agreement, to have back-up credits if some courses don't work out. Expect an uneven workload and a really long easter vacation (I had no courses or study activities for almost the entire April)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses in general were a bit of a lower level than I would prefer - I also missed a better literature list for each course (courses had 3 to 4 academic books as recommended reading with no chapter specified)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was less practical, and some of the courses desperately needed context and structure for their content. A lot of detail information was given (for example about detailed molecular pathways), but there was no information about their practical application or was it even expected to be learned for the exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Biology of aging - Exciting course about a relatively new and growing field of molecular biology
Cell factory - plants - Interesting practical course with some really flashy experiments
Practical course in environmental biotechnology - Cool supervisors and concept for an experiment, although a bit low-level
The seminars - only for easy credits, because they are very little effort and time input for the credits that they are worth

questions.answer: The registration in Vienna city must be renewed after 4 months of stay, which cost a small amount of money, but mostly it was the time spent on it

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food were more expensive than expected, but food prices are high in every country right now.

questions.answer: The University Sports Institute Vienna offers amazing, very cheap sport opportunities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The University Sports Institute Vienna

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The city has an overwhelming variety of cultural events, food festivals, hiking and ski opportunities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy, since I am from Hungary (the neighbor country) so I have cultural ties with Austria

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Socializing definitely happens while eating, so prepare for a few additional kilos to be gained during the exchange.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The food - there's so much of it!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food - it's so good!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Prepare for an uneven workload, register for more courses than you need, and don't take the exams too seriously, because the grading is very lenient.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The rules are very flexible, and there is a laid back atmosphere in the institution, so there is a great opportunity for personalization.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding experiences were mostly personal - I really liked the city of Vienna for the cultural and the natural environment, and I have met my current romantic partner.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was to take the academic part seriously - I felt that the lecturers were too lenient, and the requirements were too low, therefore it was difficult to put a lot of effort in the studies.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
